_about: Starting model for a new game (skill sonmat-new-game). Standards for combat / movement / cutscene, measured on Stellar Blade (10-09) and settled on Wukong, Lies of P, Final Fight, Cadillacs. A game only says which of its sounds belongs to which slot (profiles/<id>/game.json); tools/new_profile.py writes haptics.json from that. Every level here is a starting value: the user tunes by feel afterwards.

combat: Peak is not rationed, time at the peak is: a strong hit rises in 0.05 s, is at 1/3 after 0.06 s and at 1/10 after 0.4 s (style sb: 52 Hz body under the sound's own texture).
Only the game's biggest moments (parry / just dodge, finisher, stagger) touch the ceiling - three or four kinds per game (style.top).
Where it shakes = the rule (the sound's name). How it shakes = that sound itself, band 30-500 Hz. The drawn wave is the fallback until the sounds are prepared.
The same sound is the same strength. Weight differs only when the name differs (S/M/L, weapon).
Pad speaker: one or two kinds of moment only (parry, charge done, stagger, a signature voice), low level (gain 0.2, cut below 300 Hz), together with the peak vibration.
Triggers: only on an action that really sits on L2/R2, always with hold/until.
movement: Movement is felt, not announced. Weapon swings play their own sound, low (0.35, heavy 0.65) - this is where a game's texture comes from. Dodges, jumps, landings and plain steps stay drawn and low (0.15-0.35). None of them is redrawn as a hit (style.skip).
Plain floors stay quiet: drawn step, in combat only. Ground you feel (snow, sand, grass, water, ice) plays its own footstep sound as vibration, also outside combat (peak 0.26-0.36).
Anything that fires more than about once a second all game long is dropped or kept under 0.2.

Places are part of the first build, unasked: read the game's stage list for vehicles, water, snow, swamp. A place is a state, not an event: a bed that repeats while it lasts (profile 'beds': engine chug 0.2-0.3, water around the legs about 0.1), the steps inside it (wading 0.3), and the events at its edges (splash, the car hitting a body).
cutscene: A game that is silent in cutscenes feels half done. Every scene gets a track.
Impacts first: only what stands out of the scene's own level passes (gate), plus a little of the sustained rumble (keep 0.15). Music-only and voice-only cues are left out.
Scene peaks around 0.65 after gain (pct 90, gain 2.0); stored at 4 kHz, loaded on first use.
Nothing says 'skipped': the track ends when the player's own steps or attacks come back (not within the first 2 s).
shooting: A game with shooting in it (pod fire, flight sections, twin-stick hacking, bullet hell) gets its own layer: the action standard alone leaves these parts silent or buzzing.
My held fire is a texture, not a row of hits: one faint tick per shot, thinned to about 8 a second (rule gap 0.12), peak about 0.1. It must never mask a sword hit or a dodge.
A single heavy shot (laser, missile, charged shot) is one event: a tick or a short thump.
My bullets landing: only when the game names it apart from the enemy's bullets, and then tiny and thinned. When it cannot be told whose bullet it was, leave it out.
What matters most in bullet hell is being hit and what is about to hit: my damage is as strong as in melee; a large enemy attack charging up gets a low swell, its release a thump.
Explosions carry the kills: small / medium / large by the name.

waves._note: parts play in sequence: [freq Hz, length ms, amp, decay ms] = burst, a number = gap ms, {"swell": [freq, ms, amp]}

_wave_kinds_note: how rough each common wave is: the kind that thing is in the reference game (sonmat/data/haptic_templates.json, measured from Stellar Blade's own haptic sounds). tools/new_profile.py writes the profile's "rough" from this. The wave keeps its own pitch, length, beats and strength; only how wide and grainy it is at that pitch comes from the kind. A wave a game adds gets its own line, chosen for what that thing is (2026-10-14, never felt)

slots.look_for: perfect guard, parry, just dodge / just avoid
I am knocked down, body fall
my heavy weapon / L-size hit landing
my own heavy move hitting the ground
my held fire: one sound per bullet (gatling, flight unit shots, hacking shots)
my single heavy shots: laser, missile, charged shot
my bullets landing, only if named apart from the enemy's
a large enemy attack charging up (laser tele, charge)
a large enemy attack released (big laser fired)
my footsteps on snow, sand, grass, water, ice, glass
brushing through plants, picking up an item
ground or sea moving under you: earthquake, waves rocking a boat kitchen, a giant's stamp felt through the floor
a big creature's roar or scream (a boss)

a sound that keeps going while something is on - fire burning, an extinguisher / flamethrower / water jet spraying. Felt as long as it plays: it ends on the game's stop line (Stop_<name>), or after max seconds
cues that carry a whole scene's sound bed (goes to source.scenes, not to rules)
scene cues to leave out: voice only, music only, temp

_flags: slot flags: top = may touch the ceiling; speaker = also on the pad speaker; skip = never redrawn as a hit; drawn = keeps the model's wave even when the game's sound is there; trim = level of the clip made from the game's sound; gap = thinning in seconds; combat_only / player_control / combat = the engine's rule flags. bed = held while the sound plays: one bed per name, pulses of the wave every / vary, ended by Stop_<name> (engine beds).
_rule_sound_first: user 10-16: '음이 있으면 다 원음이지' - every slot plays the game's own sound when it has one; the slot's wave is only the fallback for an event with no clip. Was drawn (template) for: charge, stream, shot_hit, heal, dodge, jump, land, step, touch
